caveats_on_screen: Physics claims kept generic: gravity is a property of mass, cannot be switched off, has no schedule.

caption:
Earth did not lose gravity for 7 seconds on 12 August 2026. The 'Project Anchor' posts cited a leaked '$89 billion NASA document' that never existed. Gravity is a property of mass; it has no off switch. NASA and observatory officials debunked it. The real event that day was a total solar eclipse. Sources on slide 8.

#debunk #physics #gravity #science #factcheck

slides.title: No, Earth did not lose gravity for *7 seconds*
slides.sub: The 'Project Anchor' hoax of 12 August 2026, and what physics actually says.

slides.title: A leaked "$89 billion NASA document" predicted a 7-second gravity loss
slides.body: At 14:33 UTC on 12 August 2026. It spread across TikTok, Facebook and Instagram.

slides.myth: Gravity can switch off for 7 seconds
slides.fact: Gravity is a property of mass. It cannot be switched off.
slides.body: As long as Earth has mass, Earth has gravity. There is no off switch and no schedule.

slides.title: No such NASA document *existed*
slides.body: NASA and local observatory officials publicly debunked the claim.

slides.title: Three ingredients of a viral hoax
items: A **specific date and time**: 14:33 UTC, 12 August
A fake **leaked document** with a huge price tag for credibility
A **real event** the same day: a total solar eclipse

slides.title: There *was* a total solar eclipse on 12 August
slides.body: Seen from Spain, Iceland and Greenland. Real, spectacular, and not a gravity switch.

slides.title: How to spot the next one
items: Exact date, exact time, huge dollar figure: **be suspicious**
Check the agency's own website for the document
Ask what law of physics would have to break
How it spread and who debunked it: https://factually.co/fact-checks/science/project-anchor-gravity-hoax-spread-who-debunked-33cb0c
